headline: Round 1 — game feel now real in pixels (hit-stop + shake measured, not assumed). Perf fixed at root: p99 24.5ms → 5.1ms. Capture harness built: the game marks its own events so exact frames can be cut. NEW FINDING: portrait composition is far stronger than landscape — landscape leaves the batter tiny mid-frame.

bars.ref: Backyard Baseball '97 announcer density + arcade sports SFX; 1920s radio timbre
bars.measure: Event-coverage audit: every discrete game event maps to a cue. Rendered WAVs inspected for level/clipping/loop seams; in-engine capture confirms firing.
Frame-by-frame capture of all 3 pitch types; the hop must be visually distinguishable BEFORE the decision point. Window sizes measured in ms.

bars.measure: Blind A/B by fresh critic on rendered frames vs reference.

bars.ref: Arcade sports impact language: hit-stop, shake, burst, trail

subsystems.name: Game feel / juice
subsystems.bar: Hit-stop, shake, particles, trail at contact
subsystems.note: Built and VERIFIED IN CAPTURED FRAMES: hit-stop fires 3 frames @q0.96, 2 @q0.77, 1 @q0.17; screen shake measured >±14px @q0.96 vs ±4px @q0.17, so magnitude tracks contact quality. Contact flash, dust at bounce, glass at window, ball trail all wired. Independent critic reviewing now — score is provisional until it lands.
subsystems.gap: Flash reads as soft bloom rather than sharp debris; ball departure not yet legible

subsystems.name: Performance
subsystems.note: Measured, not guessed. Empty-tree floor test (0.05ms) proved the cost was ours; section timers showed script is only 0.15ms/frame, so the 24.5ms p99 was lazy per-animation texture loading mid-play, not simulation. Warming lineup textures up front: mean 6.87→1.41ms, p99 24.53→5.14ms against a 16.67ms budget.
subsystems.gap: Not yet measured on real iOS hardware

log.m: Godot binary vanished from the sandbox mid-run; restored it and added tools/ensure_godot.sh so a lost toolchain is fixable, not fatal.
NEW FINDING: portrait composition matches the reference; landscape does not. Landscape camera needs its own tuning, not a shared constant.
Independent game-feel critic spawned on the captured frames — I built this, so I do not grade it.
Built tools/capture.sh: the game prints FILM <frame> <event>, --write-movie is fixed-timestep, so exact frames around any event can be cut. No more eyeballing video.
Game feel verified in pixels: hit-stop 3/2/1 frames by quality, shake ±14px vs ±4px by quality.
Perf root cause found by measurement: lazy texture loads, not simulation. p99 24.53 → 5.14ms.
Decoupled view from art frame counts — Game.frames() now probes files, so re-timed animations stop being silently truncated.
Bars established from brief references (Backyard Baseball, Punch-Out!!, owner reference image).
Decomposition: 8 subsystems. Audio found entirely absent — promoted to P0.
Wave 1 launched: audio builder, front-end builder, animation builder in parallel; orchestrator owns match_view.gd game-feel to avoid conflicts.
